title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli spaces M_{g,ν}. Grothendieck is working out a general formalism of strata D_{α*}, their punctured versions D*_{α*}, and tubular 'germ' neighbourhoods V_{α*}, V*_{α*} attached to a space X with a (normal crossings) divisor Θ. On the previous page he computes everything in the simplest case X = E^1 (analytic affine line, i.e. C) with Θ = {0}. On this page he concludes that exactly four 'building pieces' (pièces de construction) occur.

The four pieces (264):
- C*: a global analytic space, the open stratum.
- P = {0}: a global analytic space, the point stratum, of dimension 0.
- D: the germ of open discs centred at 0, i.e. the tubular neighbourhood of the stratum P.
- D*: the germ of punctured discs, i.e. the deleted tubular neighbourhood.

So there are two 'global' pieces and two 'local' pieces.

They fit into a diagram of inclusions (265):
- P → D (the centre into the disc germ);
- D* ↪ D;
- D* → C* (the punctured germ seen at the end of the open stratum).
Dotted arrows D ⇢ C and C* ⇢ C, written in brackets, indicate the space to be reconstructed.

Claim (266): the global analytic variety C, together with its divisor Θ localized at P = {0}, is recovered as the amalgamated sum C ≅ C* ⊔_{D*} D. In modern terms this is the standard decomposition of a space with a divisor into the complement and a tubular neighbourhood glued along the deleted neighbourhood. Its homotopy-theoretic form is a homotopy pushout along the link, as in stratified spaces or the Kato–Nakayama / real oriented blow-up picture.

Purpose: this serves as the elementary model ('modèles topologiques les plus élémentaires'). On the next page he takes X = C^I with Θ the coordinate cross. He expects the elementary types there to be products, indexed by I, of the four types. He encodes them by partitions of I into four (possibly empty) parts, with the canonical maps between types deduced from (265). This is a combinatorial description of the local 'gluing' (recollement) data of a normal-crossings boundary, intended for the boundary of M_{g,ν} and its stratification by stable graphs.
errors: The pushout C ≅ C* ⊔_{D*} D is not literally meaningful for germs, which are pro-objects. It must be read with representatives (a small disc and its punctured version) or as a homotopy/pro-pushout. This is a gap in rigour only, clearly intended.

In the next page's transcription the factors of I'_1 are written as D*. Given (264), where the global one-dimensional piece is C*, they should presumably be C* (and 'gl. 5.2' should read 'global'). This is a transcription or slip issue.

ideas.what: Decomposition of a space with a divisor into four basic pieces (open stratum, closed stratum, tubular germ, punctured tubular germ) with a diagram of inclusions
ideas.modern_name: Stratified space / tubular neighbourhood (link) decomposition; recollement data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data); in homotopy form MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§§5-6, 'topologie modérée', tubular neighbourhoods at infinity of M_{g,ν}) discusses the idea in general terms

ideas.what: Reconstruction C ≅ C* ⊔_{D*} D as an amalgamated sum
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushout / Mayer–Vietoris gluing along the deleted neighbourhood

ideas.what: (Next page) Elementary types for the normal crossings model C^I as products of the four types, indexed by partitions of I into four parts
ideas.modern_name: Local product structure of normal crossings strata; Kato–Nakayama log-space local models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Kato–Nakayama (1999) for the log version

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary worked model (affine line with origin) of a gluing formalism for spaces with normal crossings divisors. The content is classical. The only notable feature is Grothendieck's explicit 'building block' categorical bookkeeping (four types, inclusion diagram, partitions of I into four parts) as groundwork for the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}. This is in the spirit of the Esquisse and of later stratified homotopy theory, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'son diviseur ∞ localisé' should read 'son diviseur Θ localisé en P = {0}' (the symbol is Θ, the divisor of (261)).
'P pointé' is likely 'P point' (P is the one-point space, cf. 'facteurs P (de dim 0)' on the next page).
In (265) the bottom row is 'C* [⇢ C]', with the dotted arrows into C enclosed in a bracket. These represent the object to be reconstructed, not part of the given diagram.
